Package io.github.kimbongjune.geoserverclient

Class GeoServerClient.Builder

java.lang.Object
io.github.kimbongjune.geoserverclient.GeoServerClient.Builder
Enclosing class:
GeoServerClient
public static class GeoServerClient.Builder extends Object
Fluent builder for GeoServerClient.

Obtain an instance via GeoServerClient.builder(). All fields except url(String) and credentials(String, String) have sensible defaults and may be omitted for simple use cases. 


 GeoServerClient client = GeoServerClient.builder()
     .url("http://localhost:8080/geoserver")
     .credentials("admin", "geoserver")
     .connectTimeout(30_000)
     .responseTimeout(90_000)
     .maxConnections(10)
     .build();
Since:
1.0.0

  • Method Details

    • url

      public GeoServerClient.Builder url(String url)
      Sets the GeoServer base URL.

      Must include the protocol, host, optional port, and the GeoServer context path, for example "http://localhost:8080/geoserver" or "https://geoserver.example.com/geoserver". Do not include a trailing slash or the /rest segment — the managers append those automatically.

      Parameters:
      url - the GeoServer base URL; must not be null or blank
      Returns:
      this builder for chaining

    • credentials

      public GeoServerClient.Builder credentials(String username, String password)
      Sets the HTTP Basic authentication credentials used for every REST request.

      GeoServer ships with admin / geoserver as defaults. In production environments supply a dedicated service account with the minimum required roles.

      Parameters:
      username - the GeoServer user name; must not be null
      password - the GeoServer password; must not be null
      Returns:
      this builder for chaining

    • defaultFormat

      public GeoServerClient.Builder defaultFormat(DataFormat format)
      Sets the default data format for API calls that support a configurable format (default and only supported value: DataFormat.JSON).

      Current limitation: only DataFormat.JSON is accepted here. Internally, most managers communicate with GeoServer over a fixed wire format chosen per-endpoint (usually JSON; a few GWC/security writes are forced to XML to work around GeoServer XStream persister bugs — see CHANGELOG.md), independent of this setting. A client-wide DataFormat.XML default is not implemented: GeoServer's XML REST responses collapse a single-item list to a bare element instead of a one-item array (unlike its JSON responses, which are consistently arrays), so the generic list-parsing logic shared by ~40 managers cannot safely assume XML today without a per-manager audit. Passing DataFormat.XML here fails fast at build() rather than silently falling back to JSON.

      XML is still fully usable where the API is explicitly XML-shaped regardless of this setting — e.g. StyleContent/SLD bodies, or the explicit per-call DataFormat overloads on individual manager methods, where you take on the parsing risk directly.

      Parameters:
      format - the default data format (must be DataFormat.JSON)
      Returns:
      this builder

    • connectTimeout

      public GeoServerClient.Builder connectTimeout(int milliseconds)
      Sets the TCP connection establishment timeout in milliseconds.

      Default: 60 000 ms (60 s). Applies to the time allowed for the TCP handshake plus TLS negotiation. Connections that are not established within this window are aborted with a timeout exception. Set lower for fast LANs or higher for remote or slow-starting GeoServer instances.

      Parameters:
      milliseconds - the connection timeout; must be greater than 0
      Returns:
      this builder for chaining

    • responseTimeout

      public GeoServerClient.Builder responseTimeout(int milliseconds)
      Sets the maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the full HTTP response.

      Default: 120 000 ms (120 s). Applies from the moment the request is fully sent until the last byte of the response body is received. Increase for large payloads (e.g. bulk importer responses) or slow GeoServer operations.

      Parameters:
      milliseconds - the response timeout; must be greater than 0
      Returns:
      this builder for chaining

    • maxConnections

      public GeoServerClient.Builder maxConnections(int maxConnections)
      Sets the maximum number of concurrent HTTP connections in the connection pool.

      Default: 50. All connections in the pool target the same GeoServer host. Raise this value when managers are called concurrently from multiple threads against the same GeoServerClient instance and HTTP connections are observed queuing or blocking under load. Setting this value higher than the GeoServer thread pool size provides no benefit.

      Parameters:
      maxConnections - the maximum pool size; must be greater than 0
      Returns:
      this builder for chaining
